page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring a single dedicated vCPU based on the arm64 architecture. Powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz, this instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports hardware-accelerated AES cryptography, though it lacks advanced vector and matrix extensions such as AVX or AMX. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the single-core capabilities of the t2a-standard-1 reside in the average tier, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1783.48 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1018.0. However, because the instance is limited to a single physical core and thread, multi-core and multi-threaded benchmarks fall into the lower percentiles, as demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 1017.0. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, measuring 11.99 GB/sec for large-block reads and 7.95 GB/sec for large-block writes.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t2a-standard-1 offers a low-entry hardware profile suitable for lightweight, single-threaded workloads. Its dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable performance compared to shared-core burstable instances, though resource density remains low. This instance is best suited for basic web serving, lightweight background tasks, simple text processing, and small-scale development or testing environments that do not require high memory bandwidth or multi-threaded execution.
